headline.purpose: Chapter title in guide sign headers.

title.purpose: Guide section openers; hub board heading at 1.6rem, loop and semester headings at 1.35rem.

subtitle.purpose: Guide h3; subject names and review-row chapter names at 1.25rem; hub chapter names at 1.1rem.

body.purpose: Reading text; line-height 1.65 in guides, 1.55 on the hub; 68ch measure in guides.

label.purpose: Buttons, home links, answer-key summary, sign course line.

chip.purpose: Course-part chips on hub subject rows.

code-sign.purpose: Short subject codes inside code squares; 1.1rem in hub subject rows, 1.15rem in sign headers.

numeral.purpose: Review-row gap values; tabular figures. Semester and loop numbers use 800 at 1.2 to 1.3rem.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: System ease-out for every state transition.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Button fills, checklist box fill, contents highlight, review row band change. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: sign-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Guide sign header padding shrinks and the code square drops to 48px.

breakpoints.name: hub-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Semester list wraps under the title; review rows, subject rows and chapters stack; loop becomes one column.

breakpoints.name: guide-rail
breakpoints.purpose: Guide contents rail collapses to a top bar.

breakpoints.name: hub-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Tick counts drop under chapter names; loop becomes two columns.

focus.purpose: Global :focus-visible ring in the action colour.

legacyTokens.purpose: Kept in system.css because css/guide.css reads them. --course is set by the subject classes (s-<code>-<step>).

extensions.borders: 2px for interactive and status outlines (buttons, home links, answer key, checklist boxes, part chips), 1px hairline for structure, 2px ink under hub section headings and over guide openers, 8px ink over the review board

subjectClasses.purpose: Sets --course on a guide <body>, a hub subject row, a review row or a code square. Lightness L 0.84 / 0.76 / 0.68, offset +/-0.04 per subject; ink labels >= 4.9:1; >= 0.08 OKLab separation between subjects under deutan, protan and tritan simulation. Same values in dark mode.

narrative.overview:
Wegweiser reads like an Ulm-school wayfinding system (the Aicher-era airport and Olympic signage) applied to a whole engineering degree, semester by semester. FAU blue enamel fields own the top of every page and every section opener; white and pale blue-grey paper carries the content underneath. Subjects are named by solid code squares in their own colour family, the same way a terminal names its gates, and semesters are numbered blue squares, the way it numbers its halls. The reader should always know where they are and what is due next.

The system is flat, square and typographic. There are no rounded corners, no shadows and no decorative motion. One grotesque family at heavy weights does all the signing. State is never carried by a new hue: urgency is a tonal band of the same blue (deep for overdue, tint for due, paper for fresh), and progress is carried by line form (dashed for not yet, solid for done or present). Density is calm and generous on the hub, and denser in the guides, where the formulas and problems carry the page. The system is built to grow: a new semester is one more section and one more jump tile, a follow-on course is the next step of its subject's colour family.

The world rejects the card-grid docs template and the hero-plus-cards hub. The hub is a sign field with a review board pinned across its lower edge, followed by ruled semester sections of subject rows; the guide is a single reading column with a contents rail.
keyCharacteristics: FAU blue (#04316A) sign fields for the hub masthead, guide headers and table headers.

Solid subject code squares in one OKLCH hue per subject (APDR violet, MEI green, EEI amber, MATLAB cyan), stepped lighter to darker for courses I, II and III, holding short codes in Hanken Grotesk 800.
Numbered blue squares for semesters and the study loop.
Square corners everywhere, flat surfaces, hairline and 2px ink rules instead of shadows.
Urgency as a tonal blue band; checklist, tick-bar and course-part state as dashed versus solid line form.
The action colour is reserved for things you can click.

rules.name: The Clickable Blue Rule
rules.body: The action colour (`--act`) is spent only on things you can click: buttons, the guide's home links, the answer-key toggle and focus rings. Signs, bands and markers use the field blue tokens (`--fau`, `--fau-mark`, `--band-overdue`), which share a hex with the action colour in light mode and separate from it in dark mode.

rules.name: The Subject Fill Rule
rules.body: Subject colours are fills only: code squares, part-chip markers and sign-header squares, always with dark ink text on them. Never set a subject colour as text, border or line colour.

rules.name: The One Hue Per Subject Rule
rules.body: A subject keeps its hue for the whole degree; a follow-on course takes the next lightness step of that hue, never a new hue. A new subject gets its own hue, picked to keep the 4.9:1 ink contrast and the 0.08 colour-blind separation from every existing family.

rules.name: The One Hue Urgency Rule
rules.body: Urgency is a tonal band of the same blue: deep field blue for overdue, tint for due, paper for fresh or new. Never introduce red, amber or green for schedule state; amber and green belong to subjects.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading as a small label. Context lines (course, module number, part, notes reference) go under the heading they belong to, at Label, 600 or regular weight in a muted or Mist colour, sentence case and normal tracking. The guide sign header puts the h1 first, then the course line, then the meta line.

rules.name: The Weight Signs Rule
rules.body: Weight, not size, separates sign from text: 800 names, 700 acts, 600 marks status, 500 annotates, 400 reads.

rules.name: The Rule Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: When something needs to stand forward, give it a heavier ink rule or a blue field, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Line Form Rule
rules.body: Progress and presence are shown by dashed versus solid, never by a change of hue alone.

dos: **Do** use FAU blue (#04316A) as the main colour, in full-width sign fields for mastheads and headers.
**Do** name a subject with its solid code square in its colour family (`s-<code>-<step>`), ink text, 800 weight.
**Do** give a follow-on course (II, III) the next lightness step of its subject's hue.
**Do** check any new subject hue for at least 4.9:1 ink-label contrast on all three steps and at least 0.08 OKLab separation from every other subject under deutan, protan and tritan simulation.
**Do** show not-yet as a dashed outline and done or present as a solid line or fill.
**Do** spend the action colour only on clickable things: buttons, home links, the answer-key toggle and focus rings.
**Do** put the guide's subject class and `data-key` on its `<body>`.
**Do** keep motion to 150ms state changes with the system ease-out, and turn it off under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** keep the legacy token names (--bg, --surface, --hl, --accent, --link, --course) in system.css, because css/guide.css reads them.
**Do** strip fills to ink text and rules in print.
donts: **Don't** put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading; context lines go under the heading.
**Don't** signal state with a new hue: no red, amber or green for overdue, due or done.
**Don't** use a subject colour as text, border or line colour; it is a fill behind dark ink.
**Don't** give a follow-on course a new hue.
**Don't** colour a non-clickable element with the action colour token.
**Don't** use the FAU logo; the site mark is its own square sign.
**Don't** build a card grid or a hero-plus-cards hub.
